n: Some converts who had been baptized in other churches asked if they needed to be baptized again. The Lord answers that old covenants are done away; baptism in his restored Church is a “new and everlasting covenant” that existed from the beginning.

f.w: a new and an everlasting covenant
even that which was from the beginning

n: Even a hundred baptisms without proper authority would not help. No one enters the “strait gate” — the narrow entrance to the path of life — by the law of Moses or by dead works.

f.g: strait = narrow; the gate of baptism leading onto the covenant path.
religious acts without divine authority or saving power.

n: Because of these dead works, God has restored his Church and this final covenant, just as in ancient times.
Enter through the gate the Lord commanded, and don’t try to counsel God about how it should be done.

f.w: seek not to counsel your God
